subject: humanities
passage: Each autumn the hill town where Lucía Ferreyra grew up holds a pottery competition that draws entries from three provinces. The rules have hardly changed in sixty years. The jury, made up of three retired potters from neighboring villages and a visiting curator from the regional museum, ______ every entry by hand before any discussion begins, turning each bowl over to inspect its base for hairline cracks and tapping its rim to hear whether the firing was even.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject is "The jury"; the long phrase "made up of three retired potters ... and a visiting curator" only describes it. "Jury" is a collective noun, and here the jury acts as a single body that follows the same rules every year. In American English a collective noun acting as one unit takes a singular verb, and the passage describes a regular routine, so the present-tense "examines" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. The singular verb "examines" agrees with the collective noun "jury" acting as one body and fits the yearly routine described.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Examine" is plural; it seems to agree with "potters," but the subject is the collective noun "jury," which acts as a unit and takes a singular verb.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Have examined" is plural, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject "jury."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Are examining" is plural, so it doesn't agree with the singular subject "jury."
